\[
s(p) > t \text{ and } s(p) \text{ is a maximum in position and scale},
\qquad
\theta = \operatorname{atan2}\Big(\sum g_y, \sum g_x\Big),
\qquad
t = 30
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(s\): The FAST score of a corner
- \(t\): The threshold
- \(g_x, g_y\): Local gradients over the long-distance pairs of the pattern
- \(x, y\): The keypoint position, with the center of the top-left pixel at 0, 0
- \(\theta\): The orientation, counterclockwise from the x axis

BRISK builds a scale space of octaves, each half the size of the one before, with intra-octaves between them. The first intra-octave is the image shrunk by 1.5. In each layer it finds AGAST corners, an adaptive form of FAST, with score s above the threshold. A corner is kept when its score beats its neighbors in its own layer and the layers above and below. Its position and scale are refined by fitting quadratics. The orientation is the direction of the mean gradient over the long-distance pairs of the BRISK sampling pattern.
